title: The Unreliable Mirror
text:
Postmodern fiction often refuses the comfort of a stable narrator. In many experimental novels, the reader is forced to assemble meaning from fragments, footnotes and contradictory accounts. Such texts deliberately expose their own artifice, reminding the reader that every story is a construction.

Critics have argued that this self-consciousness is not merely decorative. By undermining the illusion of transparent representation, writers invite readers to question how truth itself is produced. The result is an uneasy pleasure: the reader enjoys the game while recognising that the rules are never fixed.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what are readers of many experimental novels forced to do?
options: Assemble meaning from fragments and contradictory accounts
Read the text in chronological order

questions.text: What, according to the first paragraph, do such texts deliberately expose?
options: The private life of the author

questions.text: Why might critics regard the self-consciousness of these texts as more than decoration?
options: It hides the identity of the author
It makes readers question how truth is produced
It shortens the length of the novels
It removes all ambiguity from the story

questions.text: What can be inferred about the reader's attitude at the end of the passage?
options: They believe the rules of the game are fixed
They feel pleasure mixed with unease

vocabulary.translation: artifício, habilidade engenhosa usada para criar uma ilusão
vocabulary.definition: a clever or deceptive skill used to create something

vocabulary.translation: fragmentos, pedaços incompletos de algo maior
vocabulary.definition: small broken pieces of something larger

paragraph_translations: A ficção pós-moderna frequentemente recusa o conforto de um narrador estável. Em muitos romances experimentais, o leitor é obrigado a montar o sentido a partir de fragmentos, notas de rodapé e relatos contraditórios. Esses textos expõem deliberadamente o seu próprio artifício, lembrando ao leitor que toda história é uma construção.

Críticos têm argumentado que essa autoconsciência não é apenas decorativa. Ao minar a ilusão de uma representação transparente, os escritores convidam os leitores a questionar como a própria verdade é produzida. O resultado é um prazer inquieto: o leitor aprecia o jogo enquanto reconhece que as regras nunca são fixas.
